clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) Personnel system.  Prepare plans for adjusting the Federal 
civilian personnel system to simplify administration and to meet emer­
gency demands.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) Utilization. Develop policies-and implementing procedures 
designed to assist Federal agencies in achieving the most effective 
utilization of the Federal Government’ s civilian manpower in an 
emergency.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Manpower policies. As the representative of the Federal Gov­
ernment as an employer, participate, as appropriate, in the formula­
tion of national and regional manpower policies as they affect Federal 
civilian personnel and establish implementing policies as necessary.

clauses.label: (d)
clauses.text:
(d) Manpower administration.  Prepare plans, in consonance with 
national manpower policies and programs, for the administration of 
emergency civilian manpower ana employment policies within the ex­
ecutive branch of the Government, including the issuance and enforce­
ment of regulations to implement such policies.

clauses.label: (e)
clauses.text:
(e) Wage and salary stabilization.  Participate, as appropriate, 
with the Office of Emergency Planning and the Department of Labor 
in the formulation of national and regional wage and salaiy stabiliza­
tion policies as they affect Federal civilian personnel. Within the 
framework of such policies, prepare plans for the implementation of 
such polîmes and controls established for employees within the execu­
tive branch of the Government, including the issuance and enforcement 
of necessary regulations.

clauses.label: (f)
clauses.text:
(f) Assistance. Develop plans for rendering personnel manage­
ment and staffing assistance to new and expanding Federal agencies.

clauses.label: (g)
clauses.text:
(g) Recruitmg.  Develop plans for the coordination and control 
of civilian recruiting policies and practices by all Federal agencies in 
order to increase the effectiveness of the total recruitment efforts dur­
ing an emergency and to prevent undesirable recruitment practices.

clauses.label: (h)
clauses.text:
(h) Reassignment. Develop plans, to facilitate the reassignment or 
transfer of Federal civilian employees, including the movement of 
employees from one agency or location to another agency or location, 
in order to meet the most urgent needs of the executive branch during 
an emergency.

=== PDF page 16 of 149 ===
1844 THE PRESIDENT

clauses.label: (i)
clauses.text:
(i) Registration. Develop plans and procedures for a nationwide 
system of post-attack registration of Federal employees to provide a 
means for locating and returning to duty those employees who become 
physically separated from their agencies after an enemy attack^ and 
to provide for the maximum utilization of the skills of surviving 
employees.

clauses.label: (j)
clauses.text:
(j) Deferment.  Develop plans and procedures for a system to con­
trol government requests tor the selective service deferment of em­
ployees in the executive branch of the Federal Government and in the 
municipal government of the District of Columbia.

clauses.label: (k)
clauses.text:
(k) Investigations.  Prepare plans, in coordination with agencies 
having responsibilities in the personnel security field, for the conduct 
of national agency checks and inquiries, limited suitability investiga­
tions, and full field investigations under emergency conditions.
(}) Salaries , wages, and benefits.  Develop plans for operating 
under emergency conditions the essential aspects of salary and wage 
systems and such benefit systems as the Federal Employees Retire­
ment System, the Federal Employees Group Life Insurance Program, 
the Federal Employees ana Retired Federal Employees Health 
Benefits Programs, and the Federal Employees Compensation 
Program.

clauses.label: (m)
clauses.text:
(m) Federal manpower mobilisation.  Assist Federal agencies in 
establishing manpower plans to meet their own emergency manpower 
requirements; identify major or special manpower problems of indi­
vidual Federal agencies and the Federal Government as a whole in 
mobilizing a civilian work force to meet essential emergency require­
ments; identify sources of emergency manpower supply for all agen­
cies where manpower problems are indicated.; and develop 
Government-wide plans for the use of surplus Federal civilian 
manpower.

clauses.label: (n)
clauses.text:
(n) Executive reserve.  Maintain a central register of executive 
reserve members for the purpose of assisting all departments and 
agencies to avoid the issuance of invitations to persons already in the 
executive reserve, and to avoid excessive governmental demands on a 
single employer, and to assist the Federal agencies in the preparation 
of executive reserve training programs.

clauses.label: (o)
clauses.text:
(o) Training.  -Develop, organize, and conduct, as appropriate, 
interagency training programs in emergency personnel management 
for Federal employees.

clauses.label: (p)
clauses.text:
(p) Resources. Periodically assess Federal civilian manpower re­
sources available from all sources in order to estimate^ availability 
under an emergency situation, analyze resource estimates in relation to 
estimated requirements in order to identify problem areas and develop 
appropriate recommendations and programs. Provide data and as­
sistance before and after attack tor national resource evaluation 
purposes of the Office of Emergency Planning.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. Research. Within the framework of Federal research ob­
jectives, supervise, conduct, or recommend research directly concerned 
with carrying out emergency preparedness responsibilities, designate 
representatives for necessary ad hoc or task force groups, and provide 
advice and assistance to other agencies in planning for research in 
areas involving the Commission’ s interest.
Sec. 4 Functional Guidance. The Commission, in carrying out the 
functions assigned in this order, shall be guided by the following:

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text:
(a) Interagency cooperation.  The Commission shall assume the 
initiative in developing joint plans for the coordination of Govern­
ment-wide civilian manpower mobilization and emergency personnel 
administration programs with those agencies which have responsibility 
for any segment of the Federal personnel program. The Commission 
shall utilize to the maximum those capabilities of other agencies quali­
fied to perform or assist in the performance of assigned functions by 
contractual or other agreements. Plans developed by the Commission 
shall be in consonance with national manpower policies and plans 
developed pursuant to Executive Order No. 11000.

=== PDF page 17 of 149 ===
Thursday, February 28, 1962 FEDERAL REGISTER

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) Presidential coordination. The Director of the Office of Emer­
gency Planning shall advise and assist the President in determining 
policy for thé performance of functions under this order and in co­
ordinating the performance of such functions with the total national 
preparedness program.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Emergency planning.  Emergency plans and programs, and 
emergency organization structure required thereby, shall be developed 
as an integral part of the continuing activities of the Commission on 
the basis that it will have the responsibility for carrying out such pro­
grams during an emergency. The Commission shall be prepared to 
implement all appropriate plans developed under this order. Modifi­
cations and temporary organizational changes, based on emergency 
conditions, will be in accordance with policy determinations by the 
President.

clauses.label: Sec. 5.
clauses.text:
Sec. 5. Emergency Actions.  Nothing in this order shall be construed 
as conferring authority under Title III of the Federal Civil Defense 
Act of 1950, as amended, or otherwise, to put into effect any emergency 
plan, procedure, policy, program, or course of action prepared or 
developed pursuant to this order. Such authority is reserved to the 
President.

clauses.label: Sec. 6.
clauses.text:
Sec. 6. Redêlegation. The Commission is hereby authorized to re­
delegate within the Commission the functions hereinabove assigned 
to it.

clauses.label: Sec. 7.
clauses.text:
Sec. 7. Prior Actions.  To the extent of any inconsistency between 
the provisions of any prior order and the provisions of this order, the 
latter shall control. Emergency Preparedness Order No. 12 (hereto­
fore issued by the Director, Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization) 
(26 F.R. 83&-83T), is hereby revoked.

Executive O rd er 11091
ASSIGNING EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS FUNCTIONS TO THE  
CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United 
States, including authority vested in me by Reorganization Plan No.
1 of 1958 (72 Stat. 1799), it is hereby ordered as follows: '
S ection . 1. Scope. The Civil Service Commission (hereinafter 
referred to as the Commission) shall prepare national emergency plans 
and develop preparedness programs, concerning Federal civilian em­
ployees, covering : the personnel system ; personnel utilization ; man­
power administration; wage and salaty stabilization; emergency ' 
personnel management and staffing assistance to Federal agencies; 
recruiting activities ; reassignment or transfer ; a national postattack 
registration system; deferment of employees from military service; 
investigative requirements and procedures; the Employee Retirement 
System ; the employees group life insurance and health benefit pro­
grams; participation in the formulation of national and regional man­
power policies as the representative of the Federal Government as 
an employer; the establishment of implementing polices and proce­
dures for Federal personnel as necessary ; and related activities. These 
plans and programs shall be designed to develop a state of readiness 
in these areas with respect to all conditions ot national emergency, 
including attack upon the United States.
S ec. 2. Functions. The Commission shall :
(a) Personnel system.  Prepare plans for adjusting the Federal 
civilian personnel system to simplify administration and to meet emer­
gency demands.
(b) Utilization. Develop policies-and implementing procedures 
designed to assist Federal agencies in achieving the most effective 
utilization of the Federal Government’ s civilian manpower in an 
emergency.
(c) Manpower policies. As the representative of the Federal Gov­
ernment as an employer, participate, as appropriate, in the formula­
tion of national and regional manpower policies as they affect Federal 
civilian personnel and establish implementing policies as necessary.
(d) Manpower administration.  Prepare plans, in consonance with 
national manpower policies and programs, for the administration of 
emergency civilian manpower ana employment policies within the ex­
ecutive branch of the Government, including the issuance and enforce­
ment of regulations to implement such policies.
(e) Wage and salary stabilization.  Participate, as appropriate, 
with the Office of Emergency Planning and the Department of Labor 
in the formulation of national and regional wage and salaiy stabiliza­
tion policies as they affect Federal civilian personnel. Within the 
framework of such policies, prepare plans for the implementation of 
such polîmes and controls established for employees within the execu­
tive branch of the Government, including the issuance and enforcement 
of necessary regulations.
(f) Assistance. Develop plans for rendering personnel manage­
ment and staffing assistance to new and expanding Federal agencies.
(g) Recruitmg.  Develop plans for the coordination and control 
of civilian recruiting policies and practices by all Federal agencies in 
order to increase the effectiveness of the total recruitment efforts dur­
ing an emergency and to prevent undesirable recruitment practices.
(h) Reassignment. Develop plans, to facilitate the reassignment or 
transfer of Federal civilian employees, including the movement of 
employees from one agency or location to another agency or location, 
in order to meet the most urgent needs of the executive branch during 
an emergency.

versions.research_rationale: EO 11091 (signed 1963-02-26, 28 FR 1843-1845), read in full from the held official FR text: Sec. 1 Scope: Federal civilian personnel system, utilization, manpower administration, wage and salary stabilization, staffing assistance, recruiting, reassignment, post-attack registration, deferment, investigations, retirement, life insurance and health benefits; Sec. 2 Functions (a)-(p) (item (l) printed "(})" in the text layer); Sec. 3 Research; Sec. 4 Functional Guidance (a)-(c) (interagency cooperation with plans under EO 11000, Presidential coordination by the OEP Director, emergency planning); Sec. 5 Emergency Actions (no authority to put plans into effect; reserved to the President); Sec. 6 Redelegation; Sec. 7 Prior Actions (this order controls over inconsistent prior orders; OCDM Emergency Preparedness Order No. 12, cited as 26 F.R. 836-837 and printed "83&-83T" in the text layer, revoked). It has no term or sunset. EO 11490 sec. 3015 item (18) revokes it, effective on signing 1969-10-28 (official text, PDF page 95; the APP transcription was not used). Inventory: the dossier's 22 clauses omit the Sec. 1 Scope and section lead-ins and mislabel or run paragraphs together; one override restates the inventory as 7 section clauses with no gap or overlap from Sec. 1 to the end of the last section. D6 / earlier-end and later-amendment test: the OFR catalog records only the EO 11490 revocation; the OLRC note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 note records only the EO 11490 revocation; the by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds no order naming EO 11091: the hits are FR index page numbers in EO 9367 and EO 9479 and a CFR-parts list page number in EO 12593; the full EO 11490 text names it only in sec. 3015. EO 11091 sec. 4(a) relies on EO 11000 and amends nothing; EO 11000 was itself revoked by EO 11490 sec. 3015 item (8) on the same day. No order amended, suspended, superseded or ended any clause between 1963-02-26 and 1969-10-28, so no later event is attached; the 1968 statutory renaming of the Office of Emergency Planning as the Office of Emergency Preparedness (Pub. L. 90-608; not held) changed the coordinating office's name, not the life of any clause. No report deadline, transcription or strike-and-reinsert question bears on the end. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_11490 (EO 11490, 34 FR 17567-17599, official FR text of FR-1969-10-30.pdf PDF pages 63-95 held by jobs/source-ladder, read in full; the American Presidency Project transcription was not used): sec. 101 says the order 'consolidates the assignment of emergency preparedness functions to various departments and agencies heretofore contained in the 21 Executive orders and 2 Defense Mobilization orders listed in Section 3015' and that 'Assignments have been adjusted to conform to changes in organization'; sec. 102(b) charges every department and agency with continuity-of-government planning; Parts 2-29 re-assign agency functions; Part 30 sets general provisions. Sec. 3014 ('Retention of Existing Authority') preserves existing assignments of functions 'Except as provided in Section 3015', so it expressly does not reach the revoked orders; sec. 3015 revokes 21 Executive orders and 2 Defense Mobilization orders without exception. There is no effective-date, pending-matter, transition or savings clause for any revoked order. Own-residual check, reading EO 11091 in full: it assigned to the Civil Service Commission national emergency preparedness planning functions, disclaimed any authority to put plans into effect, allowed redelegation and made the order control over inconsistent prior orders. EO 11490 Part 28 (United States Civil Service Commission) re-assigns the same agencies' emergency preparedness functions, adjusted to later changes in organization (sec. 101); that is a new assignment by the consolidating order, not a continuation of EO 11091. Plans and programs developed before 1969-10-28 are completed acts of the agencies and rest on their own statutes and on the new assignment; no held source shows any of them continued by force of this order. The revocation of OCDM Emergency Preparedness Order No. 12 in its Prior Actions section was executed on issuance in 1963 and is not undone by revoking EO 11091. State transferred_or_accrued records the carry-forward of the assignment into EO 11490 and the completed acts; no clause of EO 11091 continues. Bounded search: the order and EO 11490 read in full in held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held official FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals, which hold every order number from 11091 to 11490; every hit read in context) and of the full EO 11490 text; the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); the OLRC notes (jobs/current-law USC_EO_NOTES); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

SECTION 501. Functions.

The Attorney General shall perform the following emergency preparedness functions:

  (1) Emergency documents and measures. Provide advice, as appropriate, with respect to any emergency directive or procedure prepared by a department or agency as a part of its emergency preparedness function.

  (2) Industry support.
